mechanism_narrative: The observed slight but consistent week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks indicates a nascent recovery trend that will continue, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week increase in TRANSIT mobility at t-0w suggests a renewed willingness for out-of-home travel, directly translating to increased footfall in retail and recreation venues over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT mobility increased by more than 4 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mobility does not show an increase over the next two weeks following a week-on-week TRANSIT increase of more than 4 points.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with a stabilization or slight increase in WORKPLACES mobility indicates a broader shift towards spending more time outside the home, which will positively impact retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the previous 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility continuing to decline and WORKPLACES mobility remaining stable or increasing.

mechanism_narrative: The substantial recovery in PARKS mobility observed at t-1w, even with a slight dip at t-0w, signifies a strong underlying desire for outdoor activities and public engagement that will spill over into retail and recreation over the next four weeks as restrictions ease.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, even if PARKS mobility remains significantly above its t-3w levels.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over three consecutive weeks indicates a fundamental shift in daily routines, with people spending less time at home and more time in public spaces, directly boosting retail and recreation activity over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility has decreased for three consecutive weeks leading up to t-0w.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mobility decreases or remains flat in the week immediately following a three-week consecutive decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains relatively stable while RETAIL_REC shows a slight upward trend, it suggests that essential needs are consistently met, freeing up capacity for discretionary retail and recreation spending over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mobility declines over the next two weeks, despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility remaining within 2 percentage points of its t-0w level and RETAIL_REC showing a prior upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The recent stabilization and slight increase in WORKPLACES mobility, following a period of decline, signals a gradual return to office-based work, which will incrementally drive up weekday retail and recreation footfall over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the previous 28 days, despite WORKPLACES mobility showing a stable or increasing trend.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent week-on-week increases in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility at t-0w indicate a coordinated easing of mobility restrictions and a return to pre-pandemic routines, which will broadly stimulate RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: Both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility increased from t-1w to t-0w.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing week-on-week increases at t-0w.
